rule: Every proposition an arm delivered that is NOT in continuation 3's 110-finding union is recorded here with its arm, job, my classification, the passages it cites and an explicit check against continuation 3's rejected expansions. NONE IS ADDED TO THE UNION. Adding a finding to the union is not the adjudicator's authority; these are for the Plans owners.

continuation3_rejected_expansions_checke.proposal: Marker-only conflict command is a JJ owner defect
continuation3_rejected_expansions_checke.reason: Frozen Source Control line 308 scopes legacy commands to Git absent explicit normalization; same finding withdrawn from P21/P26.

continuation3_rejected_expansions_checke.proposal: Add mutating status.refresh branch as a required correction
continuation3_rejected_expansions_checke.reason: F002 already fixes read effects and denial; a new writer-bearing branch would change that authority.
F038 already adjudicated prompt-suppressed owner helpers and foreground/background policy. H18 acknowledges unreviewed external auth-owner dependencies.

continuation3_rejected_expansions_checke.proposal: Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor
continuation3_rejected_expansions_checke.reason: Refinements/alternatives under existing F082/F086/F056 and their scope boundaries, not additional demonstrated product obligations.

convergence_clusters.cluster: Restore-drill object verification has no defined depth
convergence_clusters.note: THE STRONGEST CONVERGENCE IN THE EXPERIMENT. Two arms with different models reached the same defect from opposite directions and never saw each other's work. Arm C came from the receipt side - object_closure_result: complete is admissible whatever depth produced it, and the Backup owner already has an integrity_verification_level enum to reference. glm53 came from the semantics side - git-fsck(1)'s --connectivity-only 'will detect corruption in commits and trees, but not do any semantic checks ... Corruption in blob objects will not be detected at all' - plus field evidence from Dojjo, where refs agreed via ls-remote while the object store was torn and only a full fsck caught it. glm53 supplies the discriminating fixture: a byte-flipped blob under matching refs. Neither was rejected by continuation 3, and continuation 3's own F106 is a correction in the same JJI-008 restore family.
convergence_clusters.recommendation: The one candidate from continuation 4 I would put in front of the Plans owners on its own.

convergence_clusters.cluster: No owner-level save contract for a diff/compare or merge-editor surface
convergence_clusters.note: Three arms independently. Each proposes a typed per-path save vocabulary in place of a string map, and each states the alternative of an explicit decision to keep conflict resolution terminal-native. FLAGGED FOR ALL THREE: this is the surface of continuation 3's rejected cluster 'Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor', and much of each proposal restates union obligations (F029, F031, F033, F034, F036, F037, F056) already credited to the arm that raised it. The genuinely new part, common to all three, is that 'missing' must never be admissible as a write instruction.
convergence_clusters.recommendation: Record; expect it to be declined on continuation 3's reasoning unless the owners decide to open the surface.

convergence_clusters.cluster: A divergent change has no representable state
convergence_clusters.note: Two arms. claude-hicap establishes that the word appears nowhere in any source-control, Jujutsu or GUI context in the Plans and that node_state, the GUI graph_states prefix list and the JJ error and disabled-reason enums are all closed without it; muse13 frames the same gap as a product choice about offset-qualified targeting. F006 (identity separation) is credited to both and F022 (explicit convergence) is a union capability neither earned. Neither was rejected.
convergence_clusters.recommendation: A real representability gap; cheap to check against the closed enums.

convergence_clusters.cluster: The closure and certification records bind no version, environment or resolved path
convergence_clusters.note: Four arms, three of them review arms bounded by the same artifacts and one the full arm. deepseek41 binds the JJ tool and store-format version; muse13 binds the resolving environment and the pointer chains with their distinct bases (alternates relative to the object database, commondir relative to $GIT_DIR); Arm C binds the drill-time resolution of in-store pointers inside the isolation boundary; the union arm binds a nine-row certification scenario matrix. F050 is the behavioural rule and is credited to five of six arms; none of these is in the union.
convergence_clusters.recommendation: The largest agreed gap by arm count. Worth one consolidated owner question rather than four.

convergence_clusters.cluster: Reads must be pinned rather than granted write authority
convergence_clusters.note: Both arms land on the same side of a boundary continuation 3 settled by REJECTING an expansion. Continuation 3 declined to 'add a mutating status.refresh branch as a required correction' because F002 already fixes read effects and a writer-bearing branch would change that authority. claude-hicap requires every capture and drill read to be pinned to an exact operation with ignore-working-copy and never load_at_head(); the union arm requires a proven non-mutating observation path with typed stale results and states that 'blanket addition of writer leases to all reads would change the existing contract unnecessarily'. Independent convergence on an already-adjudicated boundary is the best evidence in this experiment that the 110-finding union is well drawn.
convergence_clusters.recommendation: No union change; record as confirmation.

candidates.label: JJ restore drill object verification has no stated depth
candidates.proposition: The backup JJ restore-verification receipt must state the verification depth that produced object_closure_result, by reference to the Backup owner's existing integrity_verification_level enum, and object_closure_result: complete must be inadmissible when the depth did not read object content, so an activation-eligible outcome cannot rest on a reachability-only pass.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. Not among continuation 3's four rejected expansions. Worth naming its kinship: continuation 3's own F106 is a correction in the same JJI-008 restore-verification family, found from the field side (a readiness flag admissible under blocked conditions) rather than the depth side.
candidates.distinctness: F081 requires complete native object interpretation and an isolated restore before activation; it does not constrain what depth of checking is allowed to produce the receipt's complete value. This is contradictory/underdetermined content inside an already-present typed receipt, the same shape continuation 3 used to hold F106 distinct from F001.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. Recorded as a candidate with evidence, as the brief requires.

candidates.label: Isolated drill must resolve and rebind in-store location pointers
candidates.proposition: Before any native command runs in the disposable copy, the restore drill must resolve every in-store location pointer (store/git_target, objects/info/alternates, .jj/repo pointer files, linked-workspace gitdir links) and record where each resolved; a pointer resolving outside the isolation boundary is a typed blocker distinct from missing objects and collisions, and is either rebound inside the boundary with the rebinding recorded or blocks the drill, never followed. isolated_verification: true is admissible only when every pointer resolved inside the boundary.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F079 requires alternate and shared stores inside the closure and F081 requires an isolated restore; neither constrains how the restored copy's own pointers resolve at drill time, and no rejected expansion covers it.
candidates.distinctness: F079 requires the capture to include underlying Git/common/alternate/shared stores; F081 requires an isolated restore. Neither constrains how the restored copy's own path pointers are resolved at drill time, which is what makes a same-host drill able to pass by reading the original's objects. The arm itself records that the clean-host condition exists in the BKP-006 lineage packet but survives in current owner text only as a future test surface.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The strongest of the five: it identifies a way to obtain a false complete-recovery badge that the current owner text permits.

candidates.label: Machine-local and ephemeral native store entries have no stated disposition
candidates.proposition: The source closure must record, for the pinned JJ version, an enumerated source-traced classification of machine-local and ephemeral entries inside .jj/repo (native lock files, per-machine store identity files) - captured as bytes but non-authoritative and never restored as active state - never a filename pattern such as '*.lock'; a version change invalidates the list until re-audited, and an unrecognized entry inside the store tree yields partial with a named ref rather than complete.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. Adjacent to F084, which governs restored configuration; this is about machine-local entries inside .jj/repo, which no union finding or rejected expansion addresses.
candidates.distinctness: F084 governs restored configuration, helpers, hooks, filters, includes and credentials. The arm states the gap explicitly: the Plans say what must be sanitized and inactive after restore but say nothing about the machine-local, ephemeral, non-configuration entries inside the store tree.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The negative test (store/extra/lockfile, store/extra/foo.lock, op_heads/locks must not be treated as locks) is the part that makes it more than a restatement of F084.

candidates.label: No blocker class for present-but-unloadable native metadata
candidates.proposition: The JJ drill blocker taxonomy needs one distinct class for a restored copy whose objects and operations are all present but whose native metadata pointers are missing or unmergeable, separate from missing object closure, conflicts, collisions, stale target and operation mismatch; any repair of such state happens only inside the disposable copy and is disclosed in the receipt.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: YES, EFFECTIVELY - and I contested it at the time. Continuation 3 rejected 'Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor' as 'Refinements/alternatives under existing F082/F086/F056 and their scope boundaries, not additional demonstrated product obligations.' A new blocker class for present-but-unloadable native metadata is a corruption-taxonomy refinement under F082. Recorded, not advanced.
candidates.distinctness: CONTESTED BY THE ADJUDICATOR. Continuation 3's symmetric adjudication already rejected the expansion 'Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor' with the reason 'Refinements/alternatives under existing F082/F086/F056 and their scope boundaries, not additional demonstrated product obligations.' This candidate is a corruption/blocker taxonomy addition under F082 and falls within that rejected class. Recorded for completeness, flagged as most likely a refinement of F082 rather than a new finding.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union, and additionally flagged as probably inside continuation 3's rejected-expansion class.

candidates.label: gc_fence_outcome held_during_capture does not state what the fence covered
candidates.proposition: gc_fence_outcome: held_during_capture must enumerate the writer paths the fence covered (native JJ process, colocated Git, registered external/automation paths) and assert that no uncovered mutation path into the same store existed for the capture window; if coverage cannot be asserted for a known path the closure is partial with the uncovered path named, and a fence claim with an empty covered-path list is rejected.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F004 states that advisory locks do not establish ownership and F079 requires the fence to exist; neither addresses a fence held truthfully over one writer path while another is uncovered.
candidates.distinctness: F004 states the general rule that advisory locks do not establish ownership and F079 requires the fence to exist; SCS-014 already rejects a lost fence. Neither addresses a fence held truthfully over one path while another was never covered, which is the case the arm demonstrates externally. Credited separately as baseline support for F004; the contract-level covered-path requirement is the residue recorded here.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. AMENDED 2026-09-16: one of the two external legs of this candidate is unsound. Arm C's claim that dojjo 'opts out of the documented mitigation by passing UNIX_EPOCH' is wrong - jj's lib/src/simple_op_store.rs:285-298 removes a file only when mtime <= keep_newer, so UNIX_EPOCH removes nothing. Verified by the adjudicator against the source; deepseek41/J0025 found it. The candidate SURVIVES on its other leg, which is unaffected: the per-instance FsDojoUploadStore io_lock that does not coordinate across concurrent HTTP requests, and the file:// remote path that bypasses the smart-HTTP handler and its lock entirely. The covered-writer-path proposition does not depend on the GC claim.

candidates.label: No record binds the JJ tool/format version a closure requires
candidates.proposition: The JJ closure record and the restore verification receipt (or a required referenced record) must bind the exact JJ adapter/tool version and store-format generation that produced the closure and the minimum version required to read it, and restore verification must compare that binding against the verifying host before emitting historical_operation_result = verified_on_disposable_copy, returning a typed blocked outcome when the versions differ outside the declared compatible range or the version is unknown.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F050 is the behavioural rule; this is the machine-contract gap beneath it. No rejected expansion covers version binding.
candidates.distinctness: F050 requires exact engine/CLI/repository-format qualification as a behavioural rule. This is the machine-contract gap underneath it: the arm read the required-field lists first-hand and established that backup_jj_closure_record, backup_jj_restore_verification_receipt and backup_source_closure_record all bind only a jujutsu_revision (change/commit/operation/workspace/bookmarks) plus repository_context_ref, that RepositoryContext binds topology and backend-native revision rather than a tool version, and that the only adapter_version in the family sits on jj_effective_capability_snapshot, which the closure records do not reference. So JJI-008 ac5's 'version-compatible' cannot be validated by the Plans' own schemas or fixtures. Same shape as continuation 3's F106/F108.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The strongest of the four: it is a required-field audit with a named validator path (scripts/pm-new-contracts-verify.py) and a fixture plan.

candidates.label: mark_conflict_resolved's text-based precondition can contradict JJI-005
candidates.proposition: cmd.source_control.mark_conflict_resolved is gated only on no_conflict_markers, so a marker-free materialized file whose typed JJ conflict is still unresolved satisfies the gate. For scm_backend=jujutsu the availability and the resolve receipt must require a fresh native conflict-state probe for the exact file/conflict identity, with conflict_state_unresolved as the blocked reason; marker absence remains a requirement only where the materialized form carries markers.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO - and it runs WITH a continuation-3 rejection rather than against it. Continuation 3 rejected 'Conflict command with marker-only resolution'; this candidate says the existing marker-free gate is insufficient for a jujutsu backend, which is the same boundary from the other side.
candidates.distinctness: F056 states the principle that clean-looking text is insufficient and native conflict state must be preserved and terminally reconciled; it is credited to this arm. This candidate identifies the exact catalog row whose stated precondition violates that principle, and names the replacement gate and its blocked reason from an existing closed vocabulary. The relation is the same as F106 to F001: the principle does not repair the row.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: The JJ command inventory has no conflict-resolution entry, so the Conflict-assistant commands have no JJ-scoped preconditions
candidates.proposition: Jujutsu_Integration.md section 3.1's 31 command IDs contain none for conflict resolution, while open_conflict / open_merge_editor / resolve_conflict_side / mark_conflict_resolved are written in Git terms (git_available, conflict_present, conflict_id_resolvable). The owner text must state that for scm_backend=jujutsu these commands require the JJI-002 revision fence plus the typed JJ conflict identity, use conflict_state_unresolved where applicable, and never require or accept a Git-only conflict_id, with the Git wording scoped to Git/worktree repositories.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO, but adjacent to a rejection. Continuation 3 rejected adding a marker-only conflict command; this asks for JJ-scoped preconditions on the EXISTING Git-scoped conflict commands rather than a new command, so it does not repeat the rejected expansion.
candidates.distinctness: F072 requires one canonical catalog with authoritative eligibility rechecks and is credited to this arm. This candidate is the specific scope hole: an existing command family with no precondition set for one of the two backends it must serve. The arm frames it as a scope clarification of existing rows, not a new command, and its acceptance check 3 preserves JJI-003's no-cmd.jj.*-alias rule.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: No save contract exists for a diff/compare or merge-editor surface
candidates.proposition: A compare/merge surface needs an owner-level save contract: typed per-path actions (write_text with expected-before hash/type, delete, create_symlink{target}, set_mode{executable}, no_change) each carrying a reason category, never a string map; typed exclusions that are not admissible targets without an explicit authorized type transition; a preflight over admission-for-this-compare-identity, parent/type materializability and capacity before the first write; identity binding to repo/worktree plus the expected native revision; application through the FileSafe ledger so failure on file N of M rolls back the whole scope or fences; and third-party tools launched over an isolated tree whose result is imported, never described as atomic when they write the worktree directly.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: PARTIALLY, flagged. It is a merge-editor save surface, which is the subject of the rejected cluster 'Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor'. Items 1-5 also restate union obligations already credited to the arm.
candidates.distinctness: PARTLY DUPLICATIVE, flagged. Items 1-5 restate obligations already in the union and already credited to this arm (F029 identity and complete matched selections, F031 byte and metadata round-trip, F033 path confinement, F034 partial writes, F037 bounded reads, F056 conflict truth). The genuinely new part is that the Plans name a structured merge editor (UI_Command_Catalog.md:549) and an external merge-tool preference (storage-plan.md:1927) with no save/write contract for either, and item 6's isolated-tree rule for third-party tool execution. Continuation 3 rejected expansions that were 'refinements/alternatives under existing findings and their scope boundaries'; the surface-level gap is the part that escapes that rejection.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union; recorded with the duplication flagged.

candidates.label: cmd.jujutsu.change.split has no expressible non-interactive execution
candidates.proposition: cmd.jujutsu.change.split is canonical, bound to a sole future handler and wired across the catalog, yet the frozen command_target can only name a change_id, and a native `jj split` with no path arguments always launches a diff editor - by default a crossterm terminal UI a Slint workbench cannot host. command_target must gain a closed change_content_selection {selection_kind: whole_change|explicit_paths, repo_relative_paths, interactive_editor: prohibited}, split must require explicit paths, a disabled reason interactive_editor_session_required must exist, and section 3.3 must state that no canonical Jujutsu command may reach an adapter invocation that can start an interactive diff or merge editor.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F028 asks for machine-readable partial-change specifications; this is the prior structural defect that the canonical split command has no expressible non-interactive execution. No rejected expansion covers it.
candidates.distinctness: F028 asks for machine-readable partial-change specifications exposed to agents and scripts, and is credited to this arm. This is the prior structural defect: the owner requires a command whose only expressible native execution is an interactive editor session that the same owner 'never describes, never blocks, and gives no typed result for'. It is a contradiction inside the frozen inventory, not a capability request.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The strongest of this arm's candidates: a canonical command with no admissible execution path.

candidates.label: An unpinned JJ read authors an operation, so capture and drill can mutate what they observe
candidates.proposition: Every JJ read issued by capture, restore verification and inspection must be pinned to an exact operation id and to ignore-working-copy (or RepoLoader::load_at(op), never load_at_head()); divergence must be probed and recorded without being resolved, with every head in operation_head_refs and a distinct divergent closure state; Backup never reconciles; and the verification receipt records the disposable copy's op-head set before and after and asserts equality, with a verification-authored operation a typed failure.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO - and, like the union arm's C4U-01, it lands on the same side as a continuation-3 rejection. Continuation 3 rejected adding a mutating status.refresh branch; this candidate keeps reads non-authoring by pinning them to an exact operation rather than by granting them write authority.
candidates.distinctness: F002 states that nominal reads have effects that must be classified and fenced, and is credited to this arm. This candidate is the specific machine-contract consequence: every PM clause about not manufacturing state names a snapshot, nothing requires a read to be operation-pinned, and all five fixtures carrying operation_head_refs hold exactly one head, so the contract is never exercised against divergence. The arm shows an unpinned read can change op_heads/heads/ even without true divergence, which makes the acceptance check a sharp discriminator.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: allowed_action_ids has no floor, so a blocked repository can admit no recovery action
candidates.proposition: availability_payload.allowed_action_ids carries no conditional of any kind, so an empty array validates for state blocked with disabled_reason_code repository_quarantined. Under Contracts_V0.md:508 recovery actions 'are admitted only when the current blocked episode exposes the corresponding ordered actions', so an empty set means no recovery action is admitted at all. A conditional must require, for the quarantine and staleness reason codes, at least cmd.jujutsu.operation.log and .show, and these must be servable from the operation store alone - without a current working-copy snapshot, a valid writer lease, or a healthy status projection.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F010 and F072 are credited to the arm; neither says an availability payload may admit an empty recovery-action set for a blocked repository. No rejected expansion covers it.
candidates.distinctness: F010 requires native and sidecar state to stay independently observable across partial failure and is credited to this arm. F072 requires one catalog with authoritative eligibility and is also credited. This candidate is the specific unbound field: the arm read all three allOf branches of availability_payload and established that none constrains allowed_action_ids, and that the one shipped availability fixture sets no precedent for the case where the status projection is itself broken.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: bookmark.track and bookmark.untrack are classified as transport mutations requiring a credential lease
candidates.proposition: The schema places cmd.jujutsu.bookmark.track and .untrack in the same conditional as git.clone/fetch/push, narrowing credential_lease_ref to a non-null ref and pinning command_class to transport_mutation, while the frozen fixture sets permission.scope to local_mutation - internally inconsistent. Native untrack and track are purely local view transactions with no remote call and no credential use. Both commands must move to command_class local_mutation with credential_lease_ref null, keeping the writer lease, FileSafe decision, permission snapshot, expected-revision fence and currentness.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F038 concerns credential architecture and F109 transport credential evidence; neither says a purely local command is misclassified as a transport mutation.
candidates.distinctness: Not in the union. F038 concerns credential architecture and custody and F109 concerns transport credential evidence fields; neither says a purely local command is misclassified as transport. The arm shows the user-visible consequence: without a credential lease a user cannot form a schema-valid untrack request at all, and the availability model would surface credential_lease_missing for an operation that never touches a network - against the product's own promise that a person can keep local history without an online service.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The most concretely falsifiable of the four: an internal inconsistency between a schema branch and its own shipped fixture.

candidates.label: A divergent change has no representable state anywhere in the corpus
candidates.proposition: A divergent change - multiple visible commits sharing one change ID - is a first-class, user-visible jj state arising from ordinary multi-actor use, and the word appears nowhere in any source-control, Jujutsu or GUI context in the Plans. node_state, the GUI graph_states prefix list and the JJ error/disabled-reason enums are all closed without it. Add divergent to node_state and graph_states, add a change_divergent_ambiguous_target reason code, and reject before effect any command whose change target resolves to more than one visible commit unless the request carries the exact commit_id.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F022 is the union's convergence capability and F006 the identity separation, both distinct from the representability gap this names.
candidates.distinctness: F006 requires change and commit identity to stay separate and is credited to this arm; F022 asks for explicit convergence of divergent commits and is recorded as a partial. This candidate is neither: it is that the state cannot be named, shown or refused at all, established by reading the closed enums that would have had to contain it rather than by literal search.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: JJI-008 states the ends of closure completeness but names no decision procedure
candidates.proposition: A JJ backup or restore path must transfer and persist dependency objects before publishing any referring head, op-head or bookmark pointer; expand and verify the full operation-to-view-to-commit-to-tree closure for the retained set including non-current, abandoned and rebased objects before reporting complete; reject missing parent files, malformed IDs, self-parents and parent cycles as distinct closure blockers rather than silent skips; materialize restores in dependency-safe order with heads and activation markers last; and activate only after the existing isolated-disposable verification succeeds.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F079 requires the closure contents, barrier and fence; this names the missing decision procedure. Not a rejected expansion.
candidates.distinctness: F079 requires the closure contents and the barrier and fence, and is credited to this arm. This candidate is the missing mechanism: the arm establishes that the Plans 'require the ends ... but name no mechanism - no objects-before-heads publication rule, no operation-to-view-to-commit-to-tree parent-closure expansion with length and missing-file validation, no topological apply order, no missing or cyclic-parent negative cases wired into adapter tests'. claude-hicap reached the same gap independently (its J0027 Gap 1), which strengthens it.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. Independently found by two arms.

candidates.label: The closure manifest records neither the resolved backend paths nor the environment that resolved them
candidates.proposition: The closure manifest must record backend-resolved store paths and the environment and inputs that resolve them, including the relevant GIT_* variables or their documented absence and which pointer files were followed; discovery must follow gitfile, commondir and objects/info/alternates chains honouring their distinct bases (alternates relative to the object database, commondir relative to the Git directory) and record each hop's base and target, with unfollowable or out-of-boundary hops surfacing as missing dependencies; and HEAD, index and working-copy material must be captured per workspace while shared commondir content is captured once, with administrative back-pointers rewritten to the disposable boundary.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. Same family as C4C-02 and C4D-01; no rejected expansion covers pointer-resolution or environment recording.
candidates.distinctness: F079 requires alternate and shared stores inside the closure and F081 requires an isolated restore; both are credited to this arm. This candidate is the resolution discipline underneath them - that the same relative path resolves differently against the object database than against the Git directory, so a single-base implementation passes today's fixtures while resolving the wrong store. The arm supplies an acceptance check built exactly on that ambiguity.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The base-confusion acceptance check is the most falsifiable part.

candidates.label: No save contract exists for a three-dir or external diff editor touching a JJ workspace
candidates.proposition: Either (A) fence any external or three-dir diff editor as a canonical command path with discriminated per-path entry types carried end to end, a save-back allowlist restricted to typed resolvable text paths under a no-follow in-tree preflight with expected snapshot, operation and conflict identity plus writer lease, Permissions, FileSafe and capacity checks, excluded bytes preserved by omission, atomic or journaled multi-file application with verified rollback and a partial-failure receipt, terminal reconciliation against post-write snapshot and conflict identity, and an explicit byte policy; or (B) explicitly scope diff.open, open_merge_editor and the Git external-merge-tool preference as read-only or built-in-editor-only for JJ workspaces with a typed disabled reason.
passages_cited: Plans/Jujutsu_Integration.md JJI-002, JJI-003, JJI-005, JJI-007:390-435, section 3.1:253-293, section 3.2-3.3
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: PARTIALLY, flagged - the same conflict/diff-editor surface as the rejected cluster, and most of its Option A restates union obligations already credited to the arm.
candidates.distinctness: PARTLY DUPLICATIVE, flagged. Most of Option A restates obligations already in the union and already credited to this arm (F029, F031, F033, F034, F036, F037, F056). What escapes that is the surface-level gap the arm establishes by literal search - no Plan names any external diff or merge tool for JJ, and the one external-merge-tool preference in the corpus is a Git conflict-assistant GUI setting 'with no safety semantics' - plus Option B, which is a genuine second disposition rather than a weaker version of Option A. deepseek41 (C4D-04) and claude-hicap (C4H-01) reached adjacent forms of this gap.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union; the duplication is flagged. Option B is the part no other arm offered.

candidates.label: Bookmark controls have the hooks for scope disclosure but none of the content
candidates.proposition: Every JJ bookmark control and confirmation must name its exact remote and action scope in ordinary words: a combined or synced presentation must still disclose which remotes are affected before dispatch; untrack on a combined bookmark must confirm all-remotes while untrack on one unsynced remote confirms that remote; rename on a tracking bookmark must disclose the untrack-first effect; delete-local and forget-remote must use distinct labels and must not share one polymorphic control without proving native semantics; push and fetch must disclose all-remotes versus one-remote; pseudo-remotes and non-fetchable remotes must not appear as ordinary remotes; and unsynced, untracked or absent refs must not be silently folded into a combined chip.
passages_cited: Plans/Jujutsu_Integration.md JJI-001:42-71, JJI-002:73-103, section 3.1:267-272, section 3.3:299-303, JJI-006:212-245, section 4.1:305-310
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F059 requires the state axes and effect previews; this is the specific finding that the Plans supply the disclosure hooks and none of the content.
candidates.distinctness: F059 requires the bookmark state axes and effect previews to be preserved, and is credited to this arm. This candidate is the specific finding that the Plans supply the hooks and none of the content: the arm establishes by literal search that no Plan text carries synced, unsynced, polymorphic, combined-bookmark or combined-chip vocabulary, so 'nothing today forces an ordinary label or confirmation to name the affected remote(s) or to distinguish delete from forget'. claude-hicap reached the schema-shaped form of the same problem (its Defect 2 and 3).
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: Divergent-change identity and draft-description retention are undefined product choices

candidates.label: A read-class PM command must not be implemented by a default mutating jj invocation
candidates.proposition: PM rejects a disabled interchange command before invoking any native helper or process, including flags that force explicit interchange; the adapter describes and gates its complete native effect scope (automatic working-copy snapshotting, Git HEAD/ref import, Git index/ref/HEAD updates, configured stale-workspace refresh); read/navigation requests keep their null mutation-authority contract and must use a proven non-mutating observation path, returning a typed stale/blocked/degraded result rather than calling default `jj status` or refreshing the workspace; successful completion requires structured native and Git postconditions, because a no-op message or exit status is diagnostic only.

candidates.label: "Object verification" has no defined depth, and a connectivity-only verifier would pass a corrupt-blob closure
candidates.proposition: JJI-008's restore acceptance says the drill must 'restore the selected historical operation with object verification', and the consumer acceptance rows repeat the phrase, but no Plan, schema or fixture defines what object verification must detect; a plan-search for fsck and connectivity returns no matches. The proposed replacement: 'full object-store integrity verification - commits, trees, and blob contents are read and checked (Git fsck default-class semantics); a connectivity-only check cannot satisfy this, and agreement of refs, bookmarks, or operation-log text alone cannot pass verification', plus a named negative family 'restore-time integrity with torn/missing objects under matching refs', mirrored into the consumer acceptance rows. Acceptance checks: a torn-pack negative, a byte-flipped-blob negative (named 'the discriminating test' because a connectivity-only verifier passes it), an intact positive, and all three across colocated, non-colocated and shared/multi-workspace fixtures. Bounded by running it once on the disposable restored copy before activation, never on the original and never while holding the capture barrier.

candidates.label: A typed per-file save vocabulary, or an explicit decision to keep JJ conflict resolution terminal-native
candidates.proposition: The corpus owns every governing principle the diffedit3 bug class violates, but the surface where the class lives - an interactive JJ conflict/merge-editor save pipeline - has no owner, command or schema: the 31-command JJ inventory contains no conflict-editing command and JJI-008 pins it unchanged, the only merge-editor command rows are Git adapter commands, and no schema models a per-file editor save state. The proposal is a typed per-file save entry referencing the FileSafe manifest vocabulary rather than duplicating it - 'text | deleted | missing | binary | unsupported{reason} | symlink{target} | mode_change{from,to}' plus backend conflict_id and expected snapshot/operation identity per file, where 'saving deleted performs deletion; missing is a scan fact, never a write instruction - the empty-vs-deleted conflation is structurally impossible' - with save validation bound to session/repository/snapshot identity, bounded preflight reads, stage-then-commit or journaled rollback, byte-identical unchanged files and a FileSafe safe point before mutation. The alternative the arm states with equal weight is an explicit owner decision to keep conflict resolution terminal-native and say so, or an upstream-first path that fixes diffedit3 and leaves the corpus untouched.
